title: Juno and the Runaway Kite
provenance: A curated fictional sample. The story and illustrations were written and drawn by hand for this demo; they were not generated by StoryMe's AI pipeline, and Juno is not a real child.

illustration.alt: Cover illustration: Juno, a smiling girl with curly black hair in two puffs, a yellow raincoat and red boots, stands on a green hill holding the string of a red fish-shaped kite flying in a bright blue sky.

pages.heading: Clover Hill
pages.text: On a breezy Saturday, Juno ran up Clover Hill with her brand-new kite. It was a red fish with a long striped tail. Up, up it swam into the sky! Then a big gust of wind tugged so hard that the string slipped right out of her fingers.

illustration.alt: On top of a grassy hill dotted with clover flowers, Juno reaches up with both hands as her red fish kite blows away on swirls of wind, its string trailing loose behind it.

pages.heading: The Duck Pond
pages.text: “Come back!” called Juno. The kite bobbed over the duck pond, and Juno followed it along the path. Three ducks quacked and pointed their beaks toward the old oak tree. “Thank you, ducks!” said Juno, and she stepped carefully across the flat stones.

illustration.alt: Juno steps across grey stepping stones on a blue pond while three white ducks look up at the red kite drifting toward a big oak tree.

pages.heading: The Old Oak Tree
pages.text: There was the kite, caught high in the branches of the old oak. Juno stretched and jumped, but it was much too high. She took a deep breath. “When something is too hard to do alone, I can ask for help,” she said. So she went to find Mr. Bell, the park gardener.

illustration.alt: The red fish kite is tangled in the high branches of a wide oak tree, its striped tail dangling, while Juno stands far below on tiptoe, reaching up. A small squirrel watches from a branch.

pages.heading: Flying Again
pages.text: Mr. Bell lifted his long fruit-picking pole and gently freed the kite. “Thank you, Mr. Bell!” said Juno. The tail was torn, so she tied it with the ribbon from her hair. Soon the red fish swam across the sunset sky again, and Juno held the string with both hands.

illustration.alt: Under an orange and pink sunset, Juno holds the kite string with both hands as the red fish kite flies high, a red ribbon bow on its tail. Mr. Bell, the gardener in a green cap, waves beside her, holding his long pole.

backCover.text: Juno learned that asking for help can be the bravest step of all.

illustration.alt: Back cover illustration: under a starry evening sky and a crescent moon, Juno stands on the hill hugging her red fish kite, its tail now tied with her red hair ribbon.
